title: Outbound request to a computed URL in python — review required
description: An HTTP client call in python receives a URL assembled at the call site from an f-string, percent-format, concatenation, or a request field. When any part of that value is user controlled, the server becomes a proxy for the attacker: loopback-only services, internal APIs, and cloud metadata endpoints are reachable from inside the network. This lexical rule sees the computed argument only and cannot prove the value is untrusted.
remediation: Build outbound URLs from a constant host, validate the path against an allowlist, resolve and re-check the destination before connecting, and do not follow redirects to unlisted hosts.
limitation: Line-based lexical match for requests/httpx/urlopen call shapes; taint propagation, redirect chains, and DNS rebinding are out of scope.
